description: El semillero de Matemáticas y Astronomía- SAROS de la Escuela de Ciencias Exactas e Ingeniería es un grupo de investigación en el que se estudia el comportamiento del Universo haciendo uso de la física, la astronomía y las matemáticas.
summary:
Future Moon and Mars missions need Earth analogs: places where astronauts, rovers, instruments and life-detection methods can be tested before launch. Most known analogs are in a few countries, so many geological environments and regions are underrepresented. Colombia has extreme diversity in a small area: deserts, dunes, active volcanoes, glaciers, salt deposits and hydrothermal springs. It is also easy to reach and close to the equator. However, its potential as an analog is barely documented and the information is scattered.

Colombia as a Gateway to Mars addresses this gap with an interactive dual-map platform that centralizes and categorizes Colombian analog candidates. The user selects a Martian site (Jezero Crater, Gale Crater or Arsia Mons) to see its context, and the Colombian map highlights the most to least similar analogs. Each site opens a panel with images and environmental data.

Similarity is calculated from NASA open data: temperature, humidity, solar radiation and rainfall erosivity from NASA POWER, plus surface temperature from MODIS via AppEEARS. Our research focuses on the Tatacoa Desert, the Zipaquirá Salt Mine and Alta Guajira.

The platform helps researchers, students and agencies find where in Colombia to test technology and astrobiology hypotheses, and opens the door to international collaboration in the region. The same approach can be extended to lunar analogs, such as volcanic terrain in Nevado del Ruiz.
details:
What it does: The platform has two linked maps, Mars and Colombia. Selecting a Martian site (Jezero: an ancient lake delta; Gale: layered sediments and evaporites; Arsia Mons: volcanic terrain) ranks eight Colombian sites by a similarity index and colors them on the map from most to least similar. Each site has an info card with an image, the parameter values and an explanation of why it is or isn’t a good analog.

Main analogs studied:

  • Tatacoa Desert: arid, eroded, iron-rich badlands, an analog for the sedimentary and fluvial landscapes of Jezero and Gale.
  • Zipaquirá Salt Mine: underground halite deposits, an analog for Martian chloride/evaporite deposits and for the search for life in salts.
  • Alta Guajira: dunes, aeolian processes and extreme aridity, an analog for Martian dune fields.
  • Secondary sites: Candelaria Desert, Nevado del Ruiz and the Tolima volcanic zones (Arsia Mons), Paipa thermal springs (hydrothermal environments) and Gorgona Island (a contrast/control site).

Data and method:

  • NASA POWER: T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN, RH2M, ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN and PRECTOTCORR. Monthly averages for 2020–2026.
  • Erosivity: Modified Fournier Index computed from monthly rainfall, using complete years only. This is a rainfall-erosivity proxy, not total erosion.
  • MODIS Terra MOD11A2 v061 (LST_Day/Night, 1 km, 8-day composites, Dec 2019–Nov 2026) via AppEEARS. Converted from K to °C, fill values excluded, median per site.
  • Each parameter is normalized and compared with reference values for the Martian target to produce a 0–1 similarity index.

Limitations (stated openly): NASA POWER cells are about 50 km wide, so they average the region and don’t capture summit conditions on the nevados. Slope and elevation (SRTM/NASADEM) are still being integrated. No Earth site matches Mars in absolute terms (pressure, cold, radiation), so the index measures relative similarity among Colombian candidates.

Tools: HTML/CSS/JavaScript, Leaflet, Python (pandas), GitHub Pages

Creativity and impact: Instead of one more analog study, we built a tool that centralizes and categorizes the analogs. It is the first catalog of this kind for Colombia, it is easy to extend with new sites, and it brings Colombia into planetary science conversations.

“Data and method”:

Site selection: The candidate sites were chosen from those proposed in Bolivar-Torres HH, Suárez-Valencia JE, Ramos-Madrigal C, et al. 2026 , which identified Colombian locations with geological and environmental features similar to Mars. We added complementary sites and context fromLeal MA, Tovar D, de Pablo MA, Bonilla MA, Bolaños J, Ruíz E, et al. 2026 and Tovar D, Leal MA, de Pablo MA, San Martin-Lobos J, Tchegliakova N, et al. 2026
